The company, the clusters, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the platform engineer at Northvale Clinics, a fictional healthcare group. A compliance review found patient data crossing between nodes in plain text, and the team wants the clinic portal's ingress moved to Gateway API this week. The cluster runs Cilium with kube-proxy replacement.
handover: Pod-to-Pod traffic across nodes is not encrypted; the clinic portal uses an Ingress with the Cilium ingress controller.
Proposal on the table: add an Istio sidecar to every Pod for mTLS.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.log: Check-in 1: the compliance team wants a plan today.
Check-in 2: the web team starts on Gateway API.
Check-in 3: the compliance team asks for evidence.

wgPrompt.title: Encrypt Pod traffic between nodes
wgPrompt.context: Cilium supports transparent WireGuard and IPsec encryption. The alternative proposal is a sidecar mesh on every Pod.

choices.label: Enable WireGuard transparent encryption through the Helm values in a rolling update, and confirm with cilium status and a capture between nodes

effects.log: WireGuard is enabled node by node; captures show encrypted traffic.

choices.feedback: Transparent encryption covers every Pod's traffic between nodes without touching the applications.

choices.label: Plan the sidecar mesh for every Pod over the next quarter

effects.log: A quarter-long sidecar rollout is planned.

choices.feedback: mTLS would work, but it adds a proxy to every Pod and leaves data in plain text for a quarter.

choices.label: Change the encryption setting and restart every Cilium agent at once to get it over with
choices.feedback: Restarting every agent at once drops connections across the whole cluster during the clinic day.

gwPrompt.title: Moving the portal's ingress
gwPrompt.context: The platform team owns the listener and certificates; the portal team owns its routes.

choices.label: Platform team creates the Gateway (cilium GatewayClass, HTTPS listener, certificate); the portal team writes HTTPRoutes with header and redirect filters; cut over by DNS after testing

effects.log: Gateway and HTTPRoutes are tested, then DNS moves.

choices.feedback: Gateway API's role-oriented resources let each team own its part, and filters replace controller-specific annotations.

choices.label: Platform team writes the Gateway and every HTTPRoute itself
choices.feedback: It works, but the portal team now files tickets for every route change.

choices.label: Delete the Ingress first, then write the Gateway

effects.log: The Ingress is deleted before the Gateway exists.

choices.feedback: With the Ingress gone and no Gateway yet, the portal is unreachable.

verifyPrompt.title: Evidence for the review
verifyPrompt.context: The reviewer asks how you know every node pair is encrypted.

choices.label: Give cilium encrypt status from every node, the WireGuard peer list, and a packet capture between two nodes showing only WireGuard traffic

effects.log: Evidence for every node is attached.

choices.feedback: Per-node status and a capture show the control works, not just that it was configured.

choices.label: Send the Helm values showing encryption enabled
choices.feedback: Configuration shows intent, not that every node is actually encrypting.

choices.label: Tell the reviewer it is done; node-9 was being replaced, so skip it

effects.log: The review is closed with node-9 unchecked.

choices.feedback: node-9 came back with an old agent configuration; its traffic is still plain text.

scoring.modelReasoning: Cilium's transparent encryption (WireGuard or IPsec) encrypts Pod traffic between nodes in the datapath, with no sidecar per Pod; roll it out node by node and prove it per node. Gateway API splits responsibility: the platform team owns the GatewayClass and Gateway (listeners, certificates), application teams own HTTPRoutes, and route filters replace controller-specific annotations; build and test the new path before removing the old.
